subject: BrightLane discovery: window sizing, streaming needs & latency SLOs
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Subject: BrightLane discovery: window sizing, streaming needs & latency SLOs

Hi Harper / Elaine —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the engineering constraints that will drive pricing and the rollout plan. I tried to break this into the concrete asks we discussed.

Recap (what BrightLane told us)
- Primary use: multi-turn policy-assistant for customer support automation (live agent assist + async summary).
- Expected traffic: peak concurrency ~40 simultaneous users, sustained 18-25 concurrent sessions per region (US first).
- Typical request size: user prompt + conversation context ~6–10k tokens; some enterprise cases up to ~12k tokens.
- Expected generated output: short answers (150–600 tokens) and occasional long-form summaries (~1.5–2k tokens).
- Streaming: partial token streaming is required for live assist use-case to preserve perceived latency.

SLOs / performance targets discussed
- Latency target (p95 generation): <= 300 ms for short responses (<= 600 output tokens) under expected concurrency.
- Tail/long outputs: best-effort for summaries, p95 can be higher (we discussed fallbacks).
- Availability: standard hosted SLA acceptable initially; will evaluate Dedicated if we hit steady-state sustained throughput.

Key technical concerns we flagged
1) Context window: 12k input tokens pushes model memory/kv-cache pressure and increases per-token latency; we need a quantized/large-window variant if BrightLane requires full-history in every request.
2) Batching vs streaming: continuous batching increases throughput but adds millisecond-level batching delay; streaming partials while batching requires hybrid handling (we can prioritize low-latency streaming lanes).
3) Concurrency economics: with 40 concurrent sessions and 600-token outputs, unit-cost changes substantially depending on batching strategy and quantization.
4) Fallbacks: canary policy to fall back to a smaller model (or shorter context) for heavy tails to preserve p95 targets.

Attachments: sample-payloads.jsonl (you uploaded during the demo) and the preliminary SLO-fit spreadsheet (slo-fit-matrix.pdf).

Next steps (ask list)
- Harper: confirm the percentile and latency target you want us to commit to for short answers (p90 vs p95) and whether streaming is mandatory for all short outputs or only for live agent flows.
- BrightLane engineering: share 1–2 representative conversation threads in the sample-payloads.jsonl format (we already have one but more diversity helps).
- Connor / Naomi (internal): run a quick model-variant matrix against the sample payloads and produce a short table of expected p95 under 3 config combos (hosted-default, hosted-quantized, dedicated-large-window) by EOD Thursday.
- Ben: I’ll produce a short one-page decision doc that maps risk/price/perf tradeoffs for the options above.

Thanks — picturing a 2-week tech evaluation (PoC) once we have the payloads and target SLO pinned.

Best,
Ben Carter

Thanks Ben — good summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Latency target: for live agent assist flows we need p90 <= 250 ms and we prefer p95 <= 350 ms if achievable. For async summaries (batch jobs) p95 can be >1s.
- Streaming: mandatory for live agent assist. Other flows can be non-streaming.
- Context: we can trim history for live assistant to last 5k tokens if that helps latency; long-history (12k) is mainly for weekly audits / compliance summaries, which can be async.

I’ll upload two additional sample threads (one live assist, one long-audit) into the Drive link you provided by EOD today. Also, is there an easy initial checklist we should run to decide Hosted vs Dedicated from a perf/cost POV?

Harper

Harper — thanks for the quick clarifications, that helps a lot. Two quick technical notes and an updated plan: 

Technical notes
- Short answers lane (live assist): target p90 250ms / p95 <= 350ms is feasible if we: (a) prioritize a low-latency serving lane (no long batching), (b) cap live-assist context to ~5k tokens in the hot path, and (c) optionally use an int8 quantized variant with the same architecture.
- Long-history audit lane: keep full 12k context, run as async job against a dedicated batch pool; we estimate p95 ~1.2–2.5s depending on model size and whether we stream partials.

Attached is the SLO-fit matrix (slo-fit-matrix.pdf) showing expected p95 numbers across three candidate configs using your sample thread (columns: hosted-default, hosted-quantized, dedicated-llarge-window). Note: these are estimates — we’ll validate in PoC.

Answer to your checklist question: short checklist to decide Hosted vs Dedicated (summary)
1) Predictability of concurrency (if peak sustained > 30 concurrent sessions -> consider Dedicated).
2) Data isolation / compliance needs (if you require VPC/on-prem -> Private).
3) Required long-window throughput (if you need frequent 12k-window online inference -> Dedicated or high-memory variant).
4) Cost cadence tolerance (bursty workload favors Hosted; steady high-throughput favors Reserved Dedicated).

Next steps (updated)
- Harper: upload two representative threads into Drive (live assist + audit).
- Connor / Naomi: run the three-config run on the combined sample set (small-run perf) and return the CSV with p50/p90/p95 and token counts.
- Ben: schedule the PoC kickoff with infra and supply a short canary/deployment checklist.

If that all looks good, I’ll schedule the PoC kickoff for next Tuesday.

Best,
Ben
